statement: A clock runs fast: in every real hour, its hands move as if $65$ minutes had passed. The clock is set to the correct time at 6:00 a.m. Later that same day, the clock shows 7:00 p.m. What is the correct time at that moment?

choices.misconception: I subtracted 5 minutes for each of the 13 hours the clock shows, 65 minutes in all, but the clock gains 5 minutes per real hour, and only 12 real hours have passed.
I subtracted only 5 minutes, as if the clock gained 5 minutes in total instead of 5 minutes every hour.
I trusted the clock and gave the time it shows, 7:00 p.m., even though the clock runs fast.
I worked out that the clock gained 65 minutes, but I added them to 7:00 p.m. instead of subtracting them.

hints: For every $60$ real minutes, the clock moves $65$ minutes.
From 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., the clock moves $13$ hours, which is $780$ clock minutes.
Convert back: $780$ clock minutes take $780 \cdot \frac{60}{65}$ real minutes.

solutions.reliable: In each real hour the clock moves $65$ minutes. From 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. it has moved $13 \cdot 60 = 780$ minutes, so the real time that has passed is $780 / 65 = 12$ hours. The correct time is $12$ hours after 6:00 a.m., which is 6:00 p.m.
solutions.elegant: Test the choice 6:00 p.m.: in those $12$ real hours the clock gains $12 \cdot 5 = 60$ minutes, so it shows $13$ hours after 6:00 a.m., which is 7:00 p.m. That matches.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
